d: The small, tough, infectious form of Chlamydia. It survives outside cells, enters epithelial cells by endocytosis, then turns into the dividing reticulate body inside the cell.
Pain when the cervix is moved during a pelvic exam, because the movement tugs on an inflamed uterus, tubes and peritoneum. It is the classic bedside sign of PID, also called the chandelier sign.

Inflammation of the liver capsule caused by PID organisms that climb the right paracolic gutter. It gives right upper quadrant pain and violin-string adhesions between the liver capsule and the abdominal wall.
The VDRL or RPR, which detects antibody to cardiolipin. Its titer falls after successful treatment, but it can be falsely positive in lupus, antiphospholipid syndrome, pregnancy and viral infections.
Giving a patient treated for chlamydia or gonorrhea medication or a prescription for a sex partner who has not been examined. Most states allow it because it lowers reinfection.

A pyosalpinx is a fallopian tube swollen with pus because its infected end has sealed shut. A hydrosalpinx is the scarred, sealed tube left after healing, filled with clear fluid, and it causes infertility.
